chunks: Ahmad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Armany from Abu Abdillah from his father from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:
The one in Ihram may kill whatever he fears upon himself.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What animals can a person in Ihram kill?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to Imam Ali (peace be upon him), clarifies the principle of *darar* (harm) in Islamic jurisprudence, allowing a pilgrim to remove threats to their safety or comfort during Ihram without penalty. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that the prohibition of hunting in Ihram is specific to game animals, whereas general pests or dangerous creatures do not incur the usual expiation (*kaffarah*) when killed for self-preservation or relief.
